source.contest: UKMT Senior Team Maths Challenge (National Final)

prompt:
Complete the crossnumber in the figure (each white square holds one digit; the number of digits of each answer is given in brackets). Answers to clues may be needed in other clues.

**Across**

1. The value of $u^2$, where $u$ and $v$ are the solutions to $\dfrac{21\text{ Across}}{5}u+\dfrac{12\text{ Down}}{25}v=478$ and $\dfrac{5\text{ Down}}{25}u+\dfrac{3\text{ Across}}{125}v=1740$ (3)
3. $\left(\sqrt[3]{21\text{ Across}}\times\sqrt{12\text{ Down}}\right)^2$ (4)
6. The obtuse angle, in degrees, between the lines $y=x$ and $y=(\tan60^\circ)x$ (3)
8. $N$ more than the sum of the interior angles, in degrees, of a regular polygon with $N$ sides (4)
10. $\sqrt{12\text{ Down}\times9\text{ Down}}$ (3)
11. The value of $p^{p-1}$ where $p$ is a prime number (3)
13. Nine more than a square (4)
16. A number so that the sum of all six digits in its row is a multiple of nine (4)
19. Larger than a fifth of 7 Down (3)
21. A cube (3)
22. Four less than the sum of a square and three times the lowest common multiple of 12 Down and 21 Across (4)
23. The sum of 600 and the smallest three-digit factor of 18 Down (3)
24. A value of $r^2+(6\text{ Across})r+21$, where $r<13$ is a positive integer (4)
25. The integer part of $\dfrac{4000}{\sqrt{9\text{ Down}}}$ (3)

**Down**

2. Larger than $1\text{ Across}\times5$ (3)
3. The difference between 3 Across times ten and 18 Down (5)
4. $N^2$ more than the sum of the interior angles, in degrees, of a regular polygon with $N$ sides (4)
5. The value of $3z^2$, where $z=\sqrt[4]{11\text{ Across}}\times\sqrt[3]{21\text{ Across}}$ (4)
7. The product of the second two-digit prime and the third odd square (3)
9. The value of $v^2$, where $u$ and $v$ are the solutions to the same pair of equations as in 1 Across (3)
12. $\dfrac{9}{125}$ of 20 Down (3)
14. The integer part of $\dfrac{2000}{\sqrt{1\text{ Across}}}$ (3)
15. The value of $10e+f+22$ where $e=13$ Across and $f=11$ Across (5)
17. A prime factor of 8 Across (3)
18. The value of $\dfrac{5(a^2-29a+154)}{a-7}$ where $a=12$ Down (4)
19. The obtuse angle, in degrees, between the lines $x=2$ and $y=(\tan60^\circ)x$ (3)
20. The value of $p^p$ where $p$ is a prime number (4)
22. A number so that the sum of all six digits in its column is two more than a multiple of nine (3)

solutions.title: Fix the easy entries, then check every clue
solutions.body:
**Primes and powers.** 20D $=p^p$ with 4 digits: $5^5=3125$. 12D $=\frac9{125}\cdot3125=225$. 11A $=p^{p-1}$ with 3 digits: $5^4=625$. 7D $=13\times25=325$. 21A is a cube, and the pair of equations in 1A only has nice solutions for $21\text{A}=125$ (with 5D $=1875$ and 3A $=5625$ below): the equations become $25u+9v=478$ and $75u+45v=1740$, giving $v=17$, $u=13$. So 1A $=13^2=169$ and 9D $=17^2=289$.

**Angles.** 6A: the lines at $45^\circ$ and $60^\circ$ meet at $15^\circ$, obtuse angle $165^\circ$. 19D: the vertical line and the line at $60^\circ$ meet at $30^\circ$, obtuse angle $150^\circ$. 8A: $180(N-2)+N=8328\Rightarrow181N=8688\Rightarrow N=48$. 4D: $180(N-2)+N^2=2356\Rightarrow N=14$.

**Direct evaluations.** 3A $=(5\times15)^2=5625$. 10A $=\sqrt{225\times289}=15\times17=255$. 5D: $z=5\times5=25$, $3z^2=1875$. 14D $=\lfloor2000/13\rfloor=153$. 2D $>845$: $918$. 25A $=\lfloor4000/17\rfloor=235$.

**Using crossings.** 18D: with $a=225$, $a^2-29a+154=(a-7)(a-22)$, so the value is $5\times203=1015$. 3D $=56250-1015=55235$. 13A $=5193=72^2+9$. 15D $=10\cdot5193+625+22=52577$. 17D: $8328=2^3\cdot3\cdot347$, prime factor $347$. 22A: $\text{lcm}(225,125)=1125$, $3\cdot1125=3375$, $3375+20^2-4=3771$. 23A: $1015=5\cdot7\cdot29$, smallest 3-digit factor $145$, so $745$. 24A: $r^2+165r+21=1587\Rightarrow r=9$. 19A $=133$ (more than $325/5=65$) fits the crossings. 16A $=8351$ (digit sum of its row $5+5+8+3+5+1=27$) and 22D $=352$ (column digit sum $6+5+8+3+5+2=29=27+2$).

**Answer:** the completed grid is shown in the answer above.
